title: After-School Care Inside Senior Living Communities
one_liner: Turn senior living's empty afternoon dining rooms into licensed school-age programs where residents are reading, repair and garden 'buddies', funded by parent tuition, operator economics and loneliness-intervention budgets.
customer: Working parents of K-5 kids near independent- and assisted-living communities (dependent-care FSA eligible, cap $7,500). Secondary payers: senior living operators seeking occupancy and retention, and Medicare Advantage plans or Area Agencies on Aging funding loneliness programs.
problem: The 3-6pm care gap is where parents lose work hours, and average US childcare costs $13,128 (35% of income for single parents). Older adults are the least-served, highest-need loneliness segment, and 40-46% of adults 65+ are 'unsure' about AI companions (Pew, Aug 2026), so a human alternative has open ground. Operators have empty spaces between lunch and dinner and no scalable, reimbursable engagement model.
solution: 'Bridge Clubs': the community lends the room 2:30-6pm. We run a licensed school-age program (1:12 ratio, bus drop from the elementary school). Residents opt into structured 30-minute roles ('Reading Elders', 'Tinkerers', 'Garden Crew'). We track participation and a loneliness scale (UCLA-3) monthly and package the data for MA plans and AAAs so they can fund resident engagement. Parents pay less than typical after-school rates because space and volunteer time subsidize it.
why_now: The dependent-care FSA cap rose to $7,500 and the 45F employer childcare credit rose to 40% (50% for small businesses) in 2026, opening employer and parent budgets. WHO's 2025 Commission put loneliness on the health agenda. Payers are hunting for measurable loneliness interventions, and school-age licensing is lighter than infant care in many states.
revenue_model: Parent tuition of about $325-475/mo. Operator rent-share or management fee. Engagement-based fees from MA plans or AAAs. Employer sponsorship of slots via the 45F credit.
non_obvious_insight: This is two 'deserts' each holding the other's unused capacity. 'Intergenerational programming' usually fails as charity. It works when the payer stack (tuition, operator occupancy, and loneliness reimbursement) makes it profitable and the resident role is a job, not a photo op.
first_30_days: Find three independent-living operators within a mile of Title I elementary schools with after-school waitlists. Run a 6-week pilot with 12 kids in one dining room using a licensed partner provider. Charge $99 registration plus $349/mo. Collect resident participation and UCLA-3 scores. Take the data to one regional MA plan's community benefits team.

title: Human Reach Audits for Newsletter and Podcast Sponsors
one_liner: Bot- and agent-scrubbed reach certificates that let honest newsletters and podcasts charge sponsors for verified human eyeballs.
customer: Newsletter and podcast operators with $5k-200k/month in sponsorship revenue on the sell side, and B2B sponsors, creator agencies and marketplaces on the buy side.
problem: Cloudflare's CEO says bots are about 20% of traffic and will exceed human traffic by 2027, with agents hitting about 1,000x more sites than a human. Opens, clicks and downloads increasingly come from scanners and AI assistants, not people. B2B sponsors buying through marketplaces such as Passionfroot and Agentio will see CPA misses and disputes, and start discounting all creators. Honest operators are hurt most.
solution: Connect to the newsletter platform and podcast host logs (Beehiiv, Ghost, Mailchimp, Libsyn, Buzzsprout). Classify every open, click and download as human, scanner or agent using timing, IP ranges, user-agent patterns and hidden honeypot links. Issue a 'Verified Human Reach' certificate with methodology and monitor it monthly, plus a sponsor-facing verify link. Later, offer pricing per verified-human click.
why_now: The bot-share trend is now being stated by infrastructure CEOs, B2B creator marketplaces are scaling (Passionfroot $15M, Agentio $40M), and reader-side detection has entered the mainstream through Substack's Pangram scan. Sponsors are getting more skeptical this budget cycle.
revenue_model: $199-499 per audit, $99/month monitoring, marketplace API fees per certificate, and a performance fee on verified-human click pricing.
non_obvious_insight: The authenticity gap that moves money is not in the content but in the audience. Sponsors buy human attention, and a certificate lets honest creators earn a premium rather than being averaged down.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 sponsor-funded newsletters via Beehiiv and Substack communities and offer a free 'what percent of your clicks are bots' scan in exchange for publishing an anonymized benchmark. Sell certificates before their next media-kit refresh, and pitch two B2B marketplaces or agencies.

title: Insurability Index and Tax-Base Hedge for Towns
one_liner: Measure insurance withdrawal town by town, then hedge municipal property-tax bases against it.
customer: Municipal finance officers of small towns, school districts and special districts in Florida, California and Colorado. Muni bond funds, community banks and rating analysts buy the data.
problem: When insurance leaves, home values fall, the tax base erodes and bonds reprice, yet nobody measures insurability itself. FAIR and Citizens policy counts, nonrenewal filings and rate filings are public but fragmented. Physical-risk scoring is commoditizing (MSCI-First Street), but insurance availability is not measured.
solution: A monthly ZIP and county Insurability Index (FAIR or Citizens share, nonrenewal filings, carrier appetite, premium-to-value), sold to muni investors, community banks and appraisers. In year two, add index-linked parametric tax-base protection backed by ILS capital, paying towns when the index crosses agreed thresholds.
why_now: Cat bonds are at record scale (about $65.6B outstanding with 12 first-time sponsors), FAIR keeps growing, and physical-risk data is consolidating while insurance availability is unmeasured.
revenue_model: $10-50K data subscriptions, then structuring fees and hedge premium.
non_obvious_insight: The financial risk is insurance withdrawal, not physical damage. It is measurable from public regulator data, and municipal budgets are unhedged against it.
first_30_days: Build the index for California and Florida counties from public data. Send it monthly to 20 muni analysts and community bankers, and convert the first subscribers.

title: Distressed Cargo Rescue Desk for Bankrupt Importers
one_liner: A broker-run desk that takes orphaned containers from failed importers, clears the four-way legal tangle in days, and delivers the goods to off-price buyers at deep discounts.
customer: Off-price retailers, closeout buyers and liquidators who cannot currently buy orphaned cargo because they are not the consignee. Carriers and CFS operators, who want the boxes gone, and trustees, who want recovery, are the supply side. The buyer pays a handling fee or a spread.
problem: When a small importer fails mid-shipment, the goods sit on the water or on a terminal with no ISF, no entry, no bond and a demurrage and storage clock running. The bills of lading are in a dead company's name. Carriers and warehouses will not release cargo to strangers. Buyers would pay well for the goods but cannot make entry. Unentered cargo can be sent to a General Order warehouse after about 15 days and is subject to public sale after roughly six months, so value bleeds out. Many boxes are eventually abandoned, auctioned for pennies or destroyed. The 2025-26 tariff whiplash left a long tail of failed importers, and Long Beach's record volumes keep yard space and free time expensive.
solution: Run a cargo rescue desk with five steps. (1) Source: call carriers' demurrage collection desks, CFS warehouses in Carson and Long Beach, and bankruptcy trustees to find orphaned cargo. (2) Screen: triage compliance risk (CPSC certification, FDA, FCC, UFLPA and IPR issues) and refuse any box that cannot be legally sold. (3) Title: obtain the trustee's or owner's transfer of cargo rights and a negotiated carrier release, trading the removal of the box for a waiver or reduction of demurrage. (4) Entry: the purchaser, as an actual purchaser with the right to make entry, becomes importer of record on a single-transaction bond, with a licensed broker filing the entry. (5) Deliver to the buyer's warehouse. Where the invoices are non-compliant, a dispute of the demurrage under the FMC's billing rules adds leverage.
why_now: Small-brand failures peaked through the 2025 tariff shock and its aftershocks. The IEEPA reversal of Feb 2026 has estates now holding refund cash but still holding stranded physical goods. Off-price retail demand for cheap inventory is high. Single-transaction customs bonds mean a new team does not need a continuous bond or big capital to start.
revenue_model: 10-15% handling and sourcing fee on landed cost from the buyer, or a resale spread on consignment goods. Add trustee-side success fees where the desk increases estate recovery. Duties and fees are pre-funded by the buyer, so the desk avoids inventory risk in the early phase.
non_obvious_insight: A container of orphaned goods is worth its inventory value minus the clock. The party that can solve four separate systems (bill-of-lading rights, the carrier lien and demurrage, customs entry and IOR, and compliance screening) in days captures the discount. VCs treat liquidation as a marketplace problem. It is a legal-plumbing problem, and only a customs broker knows how the entry, bond and purchaser-as-IOR pieces fit together.
first_30_days: Line up a partner bond agent for single-transaction bonds and one buyer network of 5-10 off-price and closeout buyers. Call demurrage collections and terminal-side contacts at 10 carriers and 10 CFS warehouses with a simple offer: we clear abandoned cargo if you waive charges. Ask two bankruptcy trustees whether any estate holds cargo. Close the first 2-3 rescues in the 30-60 day window with fully buyer-funded duties.

title: Ulysses Contracts for AI Use in Psychosis Recovery
one_liner: A patient-signed pre-commitment plus an app that adds friction and alerts a trusted contact when a recovering patient's chatbot use starts to spiral.
customer: Early-psychosis and community mental-health programs ($15-30 per patient per month) and families of people with a prior psychotic or manic episode ($12 a month).
problem: Trend chain: chatbot sycophancy leads to documented chatbot-linked psychosis (UCSF's Keith Sakata treated 12 cases; the Human Line Project spans 22 countries), then people with prior episodes are the most exposed, then clinicians can only say 'avoid chatbots' and families cannot police 3 a.m. sessions. Psychiatric advance directives cover hospitalization, not AI use.
solution: (1) A one-page 'AI Use Advance Directive' completed with the treating clinician while the patient is well. (2) A device-level app that watches patterns locally (late-night sessions, session length and, with consent, on-device classification of grandiose or mission-style themes) and applies escalating friction: delay, grounding script, message to a trusted contact, weekly clinician summary. (3) Data stays on the device except the escalation flag.
why_now: OpenAI's own Oct 2025 estimate (0.07% of weekly users show signs of psychosis or mania) implies hundreds of thousands of people. Regulation is bans and disclosures, not protection at the device level. On-device small models now make private classification feasible, and no lab has to cooperate.
revenue_model: Per-patient monthly licenses to programs (early-psychosis programs have dedicated public funding) and a $12 monthly family plan. Later: payer and long-acting-injectable partner programs.
non_obvious_insight: The winning product is not a smarter chatbot but a pre-commitment device, the same logic as psychiatric advance directives: the well self binds the unwell self. Because it lives at the device layer, it works across every model.
first_30_days: Recruit two early-psychosis programs via clinician advisors. Draft the directive template with them. Build an Android-first usage monitor (fastest to ship) and test it with about 15 patients. Sell programs a $5k pilot.

title: Buy Oil-Heat Dealers, Sell Heat Pumps
one_liner: Acquire retiring Northeast heating-oil dealers for their loyal customers and boiler-failure moments, run the fuel business as a cash annuity, and convert customers to heat pumps.
customer: Northeast homeowners heating with oil (from about 19% of homes in New York to 59% in Maine), income-qualified households with state and utility rebates, and dealer owners who want a succession exit.
problem: Oil-only dealers face policy-driven volume decline and aging owners with no successors, yet each holds 1,000 to 5,000 loyal customers with known equipment ages. Heat pump installers pay high customer-acquisition costs and lack trust. The federal 25C credit ended for systems placed in service after 2025, so state programs and CAC decide winners.
solution: Acquire small dealers, keep the local brand, drivers and techs. AI ops: a propensity model using tank size, burner age, delivery volume and home age to time an offer when a boiler is about to fail, virtual site surveys and load calcs from photos, automated rebate and financing paperwork, retraining of drivers and technicians for heat pump service, and route optimization to protect fuel cash flow during the transition. Sell 'heat-as-a-service' subscriptions with dual-fuel backup.
why_now: Post-2025, incentives shifted to state and utility programs (Massachusetts, New York, Maine and others), and HEEHRA rebates of up to $8,000 for income-qualified households continue where states have launched. Heat pump technology is mature for cold climates. Dealer owners are aging, and the customer relationship is the hard-to-buy asset.
revenue_model: Fuel margin as the cash cow, service contracts, heat pump installs at roughly $15k to $25k per job, and financing spreads. Acquisition financed with seller notes and SBA 7(a).
non_obvious_insight: Electrification's scarce asset is trust plus the moment a boiler dies. Oil dealers already own both, and they are the only local business that knows each home's system age and gets the 2 a.m. January call. Buy the relationship and use the declining fuel business to fund the conversion.
first_30_days: List 50 independent dealers within a two-hour radius from state oilheat associations. Approach five owners over 60 with seller-financed offers. Before buying, start as a white-label heat pump conversion partner that rev-shares with dealers on their customers, which can produce first revenue in 60 to 90 days.

title: Unbundling Edits for Pet Insurance Claims
one_liner: Give pet insurers the claim-edit engine human health has had for 30 years: canonical procedure codes, bundling rules, and price benchmarks for messy vet invoices.
customer: Pet insurance MGAs, carriers and TPAs adjudicating roughly 100k to 2M claims a year, the mid-size players without in-house claims data science. Later, corporate veterinary groups and pet-owner pre-treatment estimate checks.
problem: Veterinary invoices are free-text line items exported from practice-management systems, with no universal procedure code set and no NCCI-style edits. Adjusters hand-review them. Insurers cannot tell that the vet billed anesthesia monitoring, an IV catheter, fluids and the e-collar as separate lines on top of a surgery fee, or what a routine dental cleaning costs in a given ZIP code. Claim severity is inflating with vet consolidation, and insurers answer with blanket premium hikes instead of line-level accuracy.
solution: An API that ingests invoice PDFs or line items. An LLM plus a hand-built taxonomy of the top ~300 vet procedures (about 80% of spend) normalizes each line to a canonical code. A rules layer, built the way NCCI and medically-unlikely edits work, flags unbundling, duplicates and implausible units. A benchmark layer returns usual-and-customary ranges by ZIP and practice type. The adjuster sees pay, reduce or review, with reason codes.
why_now: There are roughly 7 million insured US pets, and the segment is growing at double-digit rates with loss-ratio and price-hike pressure. Corporate vet consolidation is raising invoice complexity. LLMs make invoice line-item normalization, the hard part that took human-health edit vendors years, cheap enough for a two-person team.
revenue_model: Per-claim fee of $0.25-$0.75, or 10-15% of validated savings. A 500k-claim MGA is worth $150-350k a year. Add a benchmark-data license for vet chains and an owner-facing estimate checker later.
non_obvious_insight: Every automation wave in healthcare billing started with standardized codes and claim edits, not with AI. Cotiviti and Optum are basically edit libraries with sales teams. Pet insurance is at the pre-CPT stage. Someone who has spent years living inside code sets, bundling logic and 'this is included in the global fee' arguments can build the missing layer in weeks. Insurers will not fund a fight with vets. They will fund a neutral, consistent, explainable edit that does not vary by adjuster.
first_30_days: Recruit one ex-coder (CPC) and a vet tech consultant. Build the 300-line taxonomy from public estimate sheets and a few hundred sample invoices. Approach 10 pet-insurance MGAs and TPAs with a free retrospective: run 5,000 of their anonymized past invoices and report the dollar share found in bundled, duplicate or out-of-range lines. Convert the best result into a paid pilot on per-claim pricing.

title: Blank-and-Recipe Kits for Desktop UV Printer Owners
one_liner: A monthly kit of pre-cut blanks, matched jigs and pre-calibrated height maps for the roughly 23,000 desktop UV printers that crowdfunding put into homes, so owners can fill machines and sell without fixturing trial-and-error.
customer: Owners of eufyMake E1, Longer ePrint and HeyGears-class desktop UV printers: Etsy and craft-fair sellers, keycap and phone-case micro-brands, makerspaces. Payer is the printer owner running a side business.
problem: Owners paid $1,500-$2,700 for a machine but still need to source consistent blanks, build registration jigs, tune 2.5D height maps, and finish for durability. Files are sold ad hoc on Etsy, but the hard part is physical fixturing and repeatability, so machines sit idle.
solution: A subscription that ships 30-50 laser-cut or CNC blanks (acrylic coasters, aluminium tags, keycaps, phone-case shells), a laser-cut alignment jig sized to the printer's bed, and a bundled PNG plus height map plus 'recipe card' (curing, primer and clear-coat steps) tested on the E1 and Longer. Add wholesale blank packs for sellers who want to scale, plus a 'sell this next' trend drop based on Etsy search data.
why_now: eufyMake E1 became Kickstarter's most funded project ever ($46.76M, 17,822 backers), Longer added $4.2M (1,584 backers) and HeyGears G1 $17.4M (3,911 backers). Units delivered from late 2025 through 2026 mean roughly 23,000 new owners are hitting the practical limits of the hobby now, and Etsy already has listings for E1 jigs and height-map bundles.
revenue_model: $59/mo blank-and-recipe kit, $0.40-$1.20 per blank wholesale packs (55-65% gross margin), and $19 add-on jig files. Later, sell a validated-blank certification to printer makers.
non_obvious_insight: Files are already a commodity on Etsy (e.g. 'Full Honor Set' bundles with PNG, Height Map, Print Guide, and popular E1 jigs, https://www.etsy.com/market/uv_printer_file), and the printer makers fight over ink instead. Owners' real pain is physical: one review notes prints need protective finishing, flat prints take minutes but textured pieces close to an hour, and heavy users hit ink-expiry chips (about GBP 240 of dead ink after seven months, https://www.makerhacks.com/eufymake-e1-review/), which a GitHub project was created to work around (https://github.com/joggie/eufy-timewarp). The same review says the business is 'high margin, low volume' (a keychain costing 85p sells for GBP 10-15; a GBP 5-8 tumbler up to GBP 25). Sellers who scale need repeatable blanks and jigs more than another file, and a consumable-with-recipe product is sold to them, not to the vendor. Demand sizing: https://www.entrepreneur.com/business-news/3d-printer-breaks-kickstarter-record-raises-44m/493857 and https://www.gizmocrowd.com/top-crowdfunding-campaigns.
first_30_days: Buy one E1-class printer (or borrow from an owner) and produce 3 kit designs: acrylic keychain, aluminium tag, keycap. Sell 50 founding kits at $49 in the eufyMake users Facebook group and r/UVprinting. Share before/after photos and per-piece margin math. Use a local laser-cut shop for blanks and collect feedback to lock registration tolerances.

title: Camera-Free Certified: No-Record Spaces for Smart Glasses
one_liner: A certification, signage, staff-training and radio-detection service that lets gyms, spas, clinics and bars credibly promise 'no recording devices here' as camera glasses go mainstream.
customer: Owners of boutique gyms and pilates studios (especially women-focused), salons and spas, therapist and medical practices, schools, coworking spaces and event organizers. Their insurers are the eventual channel.
problem: Camera glasses look like ordinary eyewear. Researchers and journalists have documented men covertly filming women in gyms, workplaces and beaches. New York State courts banned them from all 1,240 courthouses in July 2026, and the Air Force, DEF CON 34 and UK Comic Con have banned them too. Yet as of July 2026 no major US gym chain had a formal smart-glasses policy, and staff have no acceptable way to check.
solution: Three tiers. (1) A policy kit with signage, member-agreement language and staff scripts ($29-49/month). (2) A 'Camera-Free Certified' badge with mystery audits, listed in a consumer directory of no-record places. (3) A discreet front-desk appliance or app that passively scans for the Bluetooth and Wi-Fi signals glasses emit and quietly alerts staff. Start with the kit and badge, and add detection once there are customers.
why_now: Smart-glasses sales climbed after Meta's Ray-Ban Display launch in late 2025. In 2026 scandals reached the mainstream, Meta bricked units with tampered recording LEDs, and institutions began banning them in a burst. Venue owners now face the liability question first.
revenue_model: $39-299 per month per venue by tier, plus one-time detection hardware, audit fees, and later insurer referral fees for certified venues.
non_obvious_insight: Bans fail without enforcement, and enforcement fails without a socially acceptable way to check. The moat is the certification norm, like 'smoke-free' or 'kosher', not the detector, which is a commodity. Women-only gyms and studios are the beachhead because 'safe to change here' is a direct marketing hook, and once one studio in a town is certified its competitors have to follow.
first_30_days: Ship the policy kit and printable signage in week one. Pitch 30 boutique studios, spas and therapist offices with a 'be the first certified venue in your city' offer. Aim for 10 paying at about $39/month. Build a Raspberry Pi or phone-based BLE scanning prototype with one pilot studio and launch a simple map of certified spaces.

title: Post-Divorce Beneficiary Cleanup for Family Lawyers
one_liner: Sell divorce attorneys a flat-fee sweep that finds and fixes stale beneficiary designations, since the will is the least important estate document.
customer: Family-law attorneys and divorce mediators or CDFAs. The initial buyer is the law firm, which adds it to the closing checklist. It expands later to advisors and benefits platforms.
problem: Most middle-class wealth passes by beneficiary designation (401(k)s, IRAs, life insurance, TOD/POD accounts), not by will. For ERISA plans the plan documents generally control even when the divorce decree says otherwise (Egelhoff v. Egelhoff, Kennedy v. Plan Administrator). Clients rarely update every form. Ex-spouses get paid, second families litigate, and the lawyer faces malpractice exposure.
solution: A 'Post-Decree Beneficiary Sweep'. The client links accounts or uploads statements. Software plus a paralegal gets each custodian's current designation, compares it to the decree, will and trust, and produces a discrepancy report. It prepares custodian-specific change forms for e-signature and tracks each until confirmed. A yearly re-audit subscription follows, triggered by life events (birth, remarriage, death).
why_now: Account aggregation and LLM extraction from messy statements and custodian PDFs now make cross-custodian paperwork cheap. Retirement balances sit at record levels, and divorce among the over-50s ('grey divorce') has risen for decades. The transfer wave is putting designation errors in the spotlight.
revenue_model: $295-$495 flat per divorce billed as a firm disbursement, $79/yr monitoring, and an enterprise license to benefits platforms and advisors at roughly $1-3 per participant per year.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone in estate planning talks about wills and trusts. The biggest mis-transfers happen through forms nobody re-reads. Divorce is the one moment when a lawyer, a deadline and malpractice fear are all in the room, so it is the cheapest place to sell an audit.
first_30_days: Sell to 10 solo and small family-law firms as a flat add-on. Process the first 20 cases manually with a paralegal and spreadsheet. Track the share of clients whose ex-spouse is still named anywhere (a hypothesis to measure) and turn that into a case study and a malpractice-avoidance pitch.

title: Turf-Ban Pivot Desk for Lawn and Irrigation Crews
one_liner: A done-for-you back office that turns lawn-maintenance crews into rebate-financed turf-removal and drip-conversion contractors, and uses their weekly routes as a cheap verification network for water utilities.
customer: Independent lawn-care, landscape-maintenance and irrigation companies with 5-40 crew members in drought-restricted Western and Texas metros. Secondary payers are water utilities and conservation funders.
problem: Their core product, mowing and irrigating turf, is being restricted and priced out as drought and utility rules spread. The replacement product (turf removal, drip conversion, native planting) is a project business with estimating, permits, rebate paperwork (pre-inspection photos, invoices, post-inspection) and financing, and national outfits are taking the work. Getting customers is small firms' #1 operational challenge in the Fed's 2026 survey, and legacy local-marketing vendors like Thryv are shrinking.
solution: A rebate-stacking engine per address (utility, county, state, supplier), net-cost-after-rebate estimates, photo-guided pre and post documentation, and submission with follow-up. Bridge financing against assigned rebates. Auto-generated local landing pages, Google Business Profile posts and mailers to the crew's existing maintenance clients ('your street qualifies for $X'). A route-verification add-on where crews photo-confirm turf has stayed removed so utilities can count the savings.
why_now: 49.6% of the US is in drought and the Colorado River 2027-2036 framework forces cuts. $7.2B of FY2026 SRF money is flowing. Corporate water-positive money, such as Amazon's $20M into the Water Resilience Coalition, increasingly needs verified savings that can be counted. Lower-cost LLM tooling makes per-address rebate rules and local pages cheap to produce for a 10-person crew.
revenue_model: 10% of rebate dollars processed (rebates on a job commonly run from several hundred to a few thousand dollars). 2% per month on bridge advances. $199/mo marketing add-on. $25-$60 per site per year from utilities or funders for route verification.
non_obvious_insight: The crew's client list and weekly route are the real assets. They are the only workforce already at every yard every week, which makes them both the best sales channel for turf conversion and a near-zero-cost inspection network to catch re-sodding, the thing utilities and funders need before they trust rebate savings. The subsidy is a sales script, not the product.
first_30_days: Pick one metro with a large turf rebate program. Find 5 lawn companies through the local green-industry association. Process 10 of their pending rebates free, then charge 10%. Publish a 'net cost after rebates' page for each crew's service area. Pitch one utility on a paid route-verification pilot covering 200 sites.

title: Plaintiff-Evidence Pipeline for Kids-Tech Litigation
one_liner: Software and services that automate platform data requests, device-usage exports and chat-log preservation into court-ready per-plaintiff timelines for firms litigating social media and AI-chatbot harms to minors.
customer: Plaintiff-side mass-tort firms and litigation funders with hundreds or thousands of minor-plaintiff clients (the social media adolescent-addiction docket, the AI-chatbot wrongful-death wave). Also expert-witness firms.
problem: Raine v. OpenAI (Aug 2025) opened a wave of suits and the FTC's Sept 2025 6(b) orders raised the stakes. Each plaintiff needs account data from 5-10 platforms, screen-time records and chat exports. Families are non-technical, formats are inconsistent and firms rely on paralegals and spreadsheets.
solution: A client-facing mobile intake that guides each family through data-export requests (Google Takeout, Meta, TikTok, Snap, ChatGPT and Character.AI exports, Screen Time screenshots via OCR). It adds chain-of-custody hashing, normalizes everything into timelines (late-night usage, DM volume, content categories), redacts third-party minors and outputs expert-ready exhibits.
why_now: Trials and settlements in 2026 raise the value of well-documented plaintiffs. The volume of AI-chatbot and social-media suits (including Pennsylvania v. Character.AI, May 2026) is growing faster than firms' ops capacity.
revenue_model: $150-600 per plaintiff processed, or a $2-10k monthly per-firm subscription.
non_obvious_insight: Mass torts are won on aggregate evidence and speed, and the bottleneck is unglamorous plaintiff-level data collection. A picks-and-shovels vendor gets paid whichever side wins.
first_30_days: Contact 10 boutique mass-tort firms via legal-ops networks. Build a Takeout and Meta-export parser prototype. Charge $250 per plaintiff for a pilot batch of 40. Retain a litigation-support consultant for chain-of-custody rules. Work only through counsel, never soliciting families.

title: Solar Battery Warranty-Claim Recovery Desk
one_liner: Pool failed-battery claims from small African installers and enforce them against Chinese manufacturers for a share of recovered value.
customer: Solar installers and importers in Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana and South Africa holding failed batteries and inverters.
problem: Africa has imported more battery dollars than panels from China since 2024. Cheap packs fail, and claims need serial verification, BMS logs, RMA logistics and language skills, so installers absorb the losses.
solution: A claims desk that captures failure evidence by QR and app, files with OEMs, consolidates returns and tracks credit notes. The wedge is five Lagos importers with a backlog of dead units.
why_now: The battery import surge of 2024-26 is now reaching failure age, and installer margins are compressing.
revenue_model: 15-25% of recovered value, moving to SaaS plus failure-data sales to insurers.
non_obvious_insight: A warranty is worth only what you can enforce. Batching many small buyers gives leverage over OEMs and produces failure data that insurers need.
first_30_days: Collect backlog lists from three importers and file the first 100 claims.

title: Keep the 58-Year-Old Machinist Two Years Longer
one_liner: Carrier-co-funded ergonomic and assistive-tech programs that delay retirements instead of chasing new hires.
customer: Manufacturers with 30-300 employees and an older workforce. Workers' comp carriers and brokers co-fund it through loss-control budgets and premium credits.
problem: The industry chases Deloitte and Manufacturing Institute's 3.8M hires needed by 2033, with 1.9M possibly unfilled. Their 2024 report stresses retention, not just applicants. About 60% of manufacturing firms have owners aged 55+. Each retiring senior machinist takes years of tacit skill, and recruiting and training replacements is slow and costly.
solution: A 90-day Longevity Program. It starts with an ergonomic assessment of every role held by workers aged 50+. Then it installs a kit of lift assists, tilting fixtures, better lighting and vibration-damped tool holders, plus optional exoskeleton pilots for overhead work. It also designs phased-retirement roles (for example, mentor three days a week). It tracks injuries and retention against a baseline.
why_now: Manufacturing jobs are up 58k since the December 2025 low, so labor is tightening. Announced reshoring hires land 12-24 months after announcements. Lift-assist and exoskeleton hardware is now cheap enough for small shops.
revenue_model: $8-25k per program plus about $150 per employee per month for monitoring and a training-video library. Finder fees from carriers. Optional performance pricing tied to retention.
non_obvious_insight: The cheapest hire is the one who does not retire. Insurers already fund loss control for exactly this age group, so the shop's cost is partly paid by a third party with a matching incentive. My rough estimate is that one avoided senior-machinist retirement is worth well over $100k in replacement, scrap and customer risk.
first_30_days: Call loss-control reps at three regional workers' comp carriers or brokers. Offer three free shop assessments. Document before-and-after injury and absence data. Use the results to sell paid programs to the shops.

title: Install-and-Map Crew for Crowdfunded Yard Robots
one_liner: A local white-glove setup and seasonal-care service for the $4-5K yard robots that Kickstarter backers are buying and struggling to get working.
customer: Owners of $2,200-$5,500 crowdfunded or prosumer yard robots (Yarbo M and similar): affluent suburban homeowners with 0.5-2 acres, seniors who cannot lift a 200 lb unit, and small landscaping and snow-removal firms. Payer is the homeowner or firm, with an installer-referral fee from manufacturers or resellers as a later option.
problem: Big-ticket crowdfunded robots ship as a Shenzhen-supported product that takes multiple weekends to set up: RTK antenna placement, GPS calibration, yard mapping, no-go zones, firmware chasing. It weighs about 200 lb, and owners report escalations without resolution from a China-based support team.
solution: A certified two-person install crew that does a one-visit RTK site survey (satellite-visibility check, antenna mounting), lifts and assembles the unit, maps the yard, sets zones and snow paths, and hands off with a 30-day check-in. Add a $19/mo seasonal-care plan covering firmware updates, blade and attachment swaps, and pre-winter snow-blower setup. Start with Yarbo, then extend to other $3K+ crowdfunded home robots and ultra-short-throw laser projectors (5,260 backers took the $2,999 XGIMI tier).
why_now: Yarbo M backers were told to expect delivery from August 2026, and snow-blower-module backers ship mid-November, right before the season the module exists for. That gives a hard deadline in autumn 2026. Wire-free RTK robots are only now cheap enough for homeowners, and the seniors and heavy-yard buyers who most need help are exactly the ones who cannot self-install.
revenue_model: $399-$799 per install visit (higher for wooded or complex lots), $19/mo or $149/yr seasonal-care plan, and $99-$199 per attachment swap or spring/fall visit. Optional B2B contracts for landscapers converting to robot fleets.
non_obvious_insight: The Kickstarter tech median pledge is $194, but this robot's backers average over $4,000 each ($3,158,140 from 751 backers, https://www.gizmocrowd.com/post/yarbo-m-yard-robot). At that price the buyer is effectively a serviced-equipment customer, not a gadget hobbyist. Hands-on reviews say setup took multiple weekends, the unit weighs about 200 lb (owners "could not have set the unit up alone"), GPS struggles under tree cover, support runs from China with East Coast friction, and the maker declined Home Assistant API access in March 2025 (https://seekandscore.com/yarbo-review/). Crowdfunded hardware makers optimise for shipping units, not last-mile success, so the installer layer is unowned. It is a local-services business with software-like repeat revenue.
first_30_days: Read public Kickstarter and Yarbo forum comments to find backers in snow-belt ZIP codes, and post in the Yarbo owner communities offering a founding-customer $299 install. Recruit 2-3 landscapers or handymen who already own a truck and lift gear. Run 5 paid installs on your own or friends' properties to write a mapping and RTK-survey checklist, then film one before/after case study. Book 15-20 installs timed to the November snow-blower shipments and sign one landscaping firm to a pilot contract.

title: Cross-Border Clearinghouse for VTuber Merch
one_liner: A duty-paid storefront and fulfillment rail for VTuber agencies that pre-sells to overseas fans and clears unsold Japanese inventory to them.
customer: Mid-size and independent VTuber and idol agencies (not Cover or Anycolor initially), plus overseas fans buying from a duty-paid storefront.
problem: Cover Corp's FY3/2026 revenue rose 13.7% but net profit fell 45.7%, hit by 1.8B yen of unsold merch and a 3.3B yen metaverse write-off. Overseas viewers are about 30% of viewership and roughly 10B yen of revenue, yet those fans face customs surprises, region-locked stores and 30-100% proxy markups.
solution: A global storefront and fulfillment layer with duty-paid shipping, pre-order demand aggregation, and Japanese warehouse partners. Overseas pre-order counts feed manufacturing quantities to reduce overproduction. Overstock is bought or consigned and resold to overseas fans with authenticity guarantees.
why_now: The US ended its $800 de minimis exemption in Aug 2025 and the EU is moving the same way, which breaks the old cheap-parcel proxy model. Hololive's profit drop is a public case study in overproduction.
revenue_model: 15-25% commission on gross merchandise value plus fulfillment fees, and 25-40% of wholesale margin on bought overstock.
non_obvious_insight: Overproduction in Japan and unmet demand overseas are two sides of one imbalance. Forecasts miss overseas demand because logistics hide it, so a clearinghouse converts waste into revenue and generates a better forecast from pre-orders.
first_30_days: Contact 10 small VTuber agencies and 3 Japanese merch producers. Launch a 50-SKU duty-paid shop for one agency. Line up a Japan-based fulfillment partner and pre-sell to an overseas fan community.

title: Show Safe: Compliance and Theft Registry
one_liner: An operating layer for card-show and fan-convention promoters that handles vendor tax permits, insurance certificates, secure check-in and a shared stolen-slab registry.
customer: Promoters of card shows, comic and anime cons (thousands across the US) and vendor associations.
problem: State rules put promoters on the hook for collecting tax on admissions and verifying vendor permits (RI, NY and TX guidance). Armed robberies and thefts of collectors and vendors spiked in 2026 (CNN, April 2026; $100k stolen from a Burbank card store; about $10k stolen at Anime NYC). Promoters run on spreadsheets and Facebook groups.
solution: Vendor onboarding with per-state permit and tax-ID verification and insurance certificate upload, table booking and payments, badge check-in and out logs, incident reporting, and a registry of stolen graded-card cert numbers and serials that vendors and stores can scan-check. Optional admissions-tax filing.
why_now: The 2026 theft wave and insurer scrutiny make promoters want safety and paperwork rigor. The registry's value grows with every show that joins.
revenue_model: $150-500 per show SaaS, ~1.5% on payments, registry API access for stores, and insurance referrals.
non_obvious_insight: Promoters are the choke point where thousands of vendors meet, so the stolen-goods network effect belongs to whoever sees vendor flow. Compliance is the reason to sign up, and the registry is the moat.
first_30_days: Sign 10 local promoters with a free first show. Seed the registry from public theft reports on social media. Charge from show two.

title: Pre-Permitted Gateway Campuses for Satellite Constellations
one_liner: A real-estate developer for multi-tenant satellite gateway sites with power, fiber, interference studies and landing-right support.
customer: Constellation operators (broadband, direct-to-cell, EO downlink) that need dozens of gateways in many countries, and ground-station-as-a-service providers.
problem: Every constellation needs gateways that are radio-quiet, low in rain fade, and connected to fiber and power. Zoning, community opposition and national landing rights make site acquisition slow, and launching more satellites does not help if gateways are the bottleneck. AST is launch-constrained now, but ground capacity is next.
solution: Option, entitle and pre-permit 'gateway campuses' in strategic regions, then lease antenna pads on 10-15 year terms. Include interference and rain-fade studies, fiber and power, and local licensing help. Start in the Caribbean, Latin America and Africa, where landing rights and site scarcity bind hardest.
why_now: Launch capacity is exploding, so the bottleneck shifts to the ground. Spectrum is now owned by operators with big plans (SpaceX, AT&T, AST). Direct-to-cell needs many gateways to reach many carriers.
revenue_model: Pad leases $8-25k per month per antenna. Development fee on entitlement assignment. Long-term power and fiber pass-through margin.
non_obvious_insight: Operators over-invest in satellites and under-invest in the boring ground sites that gate capacity. Zoning boards, not rockets, may be the binding constraint.
first_30_days: Use GIS to shortlist 30 parcels near fiber and power across five regions. Take low-cost options on five. Get LOIs from two gateway-hungry operators or teleport providers before spending on entitlements.

title: Laid-Off Auto Technicians to Water Operators
one_liner: A paid-placement training pipeline that turns displaced auto and machinery technicians into licensed water and wastewater operators.
customer: Contract water operators and small utilities, paying $4-8k per placed operator. State dislocated-worker and WIOA funds cover much of the tuition.
problem: Water systems face retirements, PFAS, nitrate and 2027 lead-and-copper deadlines with too few skilled operators. Meanwhile auto OEM robot orders are down 25% and autos lost 4.5k jobs in August, while the industrial maintenance and PLC skills those workers hold are what treatment plants cannot find.
solution: An 8-12 week bootcamp that maps PLC, pump, motor and controls skills onto Grade 1-2 operator exams plus PFAS media, ion exchange and membrane basics. Each trainee has a conditional job offer as an operator-in-training before starting. Solve the experience-hours bottleneck through contract-operator trainee slots.
why_now: Auto and metals layoffs are running alongside record capital-goods orders. Compliance clocks (PFAS monitoring 2027, LCRI Nov 2027) force hiring now, and EPA money for treatment is flowing.
revenue_model: Placement fee per hire from employers, plus state workforce-fund tuition reimbursement. Optional income-share for trainees.
non_obvious_insight: The binding constraint on water treatment is not money. It is people who can keep a PLC-run plant alive, and shrinking auto plants hold exactly those people.
first_30_days: Contact state Rapid Response teams for two Midwest auto-plant layoffs. Sign one contract operator for 10 conditional offers. Run a first cohort of 12 with a community-college partner.

title: Texas Data-Center Water Filing and Attestation
one_liner: A fixed-fee compliance service that meters, calculates, files and PE-attests data-center water reports for the operators who ignored Texas's mandatory water survey.
customer: About 280 non-responding Texas data centers (colos, crypto miners, enterprise sites, edge facilities) and developers of the roughly 1,800 projects held in the ERCOT queue. The operator or developer pays.
problem: Only 17% of 341 surveyed Texas data centers answered the mandatory 2025 water survey (maximum fine $500). On Aug 3 the governor froze ERCOT connection approvals pending a water and energy audit, and TWDB owes an update by Oct 14, 2026. Non-reporting is about to become a crime and a bar to TCEQ permits and interconnection. Small operators have no in-house water or regulatory staff.
solution: A turnkey filing: interpret the survey, verify or install non-invasive clamp-on flow metering on make-up and blowdown lines, reconcile utility bills, compute WUE plus scarcity-adjusted and grid-indirect water, then have a Texas licensed PE sign an attestation. Keep an audit-ready data room and issue quarterly updates as rules change.
why_now: The freeze, the Oct 14 update and the coming criminal penalties all land within weeks. A stamp from an independent PE unblocks permits and interconnection, and nobody else sells it to the long tail.
revenue_model: $5-15k per-facility filing package, $2-5k/month recurring attestation, $50-200k portfolio deals. Anonymized data becomes the first scarcity-adjusted benchmark set.
non_obvious_insight: The hyperscalers will self-certify. The 83% who did not respond, mostly small and mid-size operators, will be the first enforcement targets. Enforcement demand arrives suddenly, and whoever has met 50 operators and installed 50 meters in the first wave owns the reference dataset.
first_30_days: Build a list of Texas data centers from public survey and ERCOT queue records. Partner with a Texas engineering firm for PE stamps. Host a 'what to do before Oct 14' webinar, cold-email 100 non-responders, and close the first five filings at $5-10k.

title: Camera-to-Courtroom Evidence Provenance for Small Firms
one_liner: A capture app and export service that timestamps and cryptographically signs photos, video, texts and voicemails at collection, packaged with an authentication affidavit for court.
customer: Family-law, employment, landlord-tenant and personal-injury firms with up to 10 attorneys, their clients, legal-aid groups and HR investigators.
problem: Deepfakes make every screenshot and clip attackable. Courts and rule-makers are debating standards for machine-generated and possibly fabricated evidence (background, verify), and opposing counsel increasingly says 'that could be AI'. Honest clients then need a forensic expert at thousands of dollars per item to prove authenticity.
solution: Mobile capture that uses C2PA Content Credentials where phones support them (Pixel 10 added camera-level signing in 2025, background, verify) with a fallback for other devices, an SMS, WhatsApp and iMessage exporter with hash chaining, RFC 3161 trusted timestamps, chain-of-custody logs, and a one-click authentication package with a declaration template and a verifier page for the court. Optional expert-declaration add-on.
why_now: Mainstream phones gained hardware-backed provenance in 2025, judicial scrutiny of AI-generated evidence rose through 2025-26, and timestamping and signing infrastructure is now near-free.
revenue_model: $9-29 per case pack, $99-299/month per firm, and $250-500 per expert add-on.
non_obvious_insight: The generative-AI problem for law is not only fake evidence getting in, but real evidence being dismissed. Provenance at creation is a right-of-reply tool for the party with fewer resources, so the customer is the weaker litigant's lawyer.
first_30_days: Ship the capture app and message exporter, pilot with 15 family-law solos, get a forensic examiner to co-sign the package and stage a mock authentication hearing with a law-school clinic. Charge $99/month afterward.

title: Rainbows End Book Scanning With Chain of Custody
one_liner: Vernor Vinge's destructive mass digitization of a library, run as a service where the AI customer is owner of record and gets clean text plus a custody certificate, never resold scans.
customer: Specialist and mid-tier model builders (legal, medical, engineering and regional-language models) and enterprises training internal models. The buyer is the head of data or general counsel.
problem: After the Bartz v. Anthropic ruling (fair use for buying and scanning print books) and the $1.5 billion settlement over pirated copies, buy-and-scan is the defensible path. But it takes procurement across thousands of sellers, cutters, production scanners, QA and custody records. Only frontier labs have that muscle (the Project Panama disclosures in 2026 showed how large it was).
solution: Acquire books on the customer's behalf under a bill of sale so the customer is owner of record. Scan under work-for-hire, deliver OCR text and a chain-of-custody ledger (ISBN, invoice, copy serial number, cut and pulp certificate), and retain no digital copies. Focus on niches frontier labs skip: out-of-print trade and technical manuals, legal treatises, closing corporate and law-firm libraries, university deaccessions and regional-language books. A rare-edition triage rule sends scarce books to libraries or an archive instead of the cutter.
why_now: The Project Panama disclosures, the 2025 settlement and public backlash over 'book burning' have made provenance a line item for legal teams. Specialist labs want clean data but lack ops. Production scanners and hydraulic cutters are cheap and off the shelf.
revenue_model: Per-book fee (about $1.50-3), acquisition cost pass-through plus 10-20% procurement margin, typically $25-100k per project, plus a premium for custody-certificate audits.
non_obvious_insight: The Bartz reasoning covers a lab scanning books it owns for its own training, not reselling the scans. The whole business must therefore be structured as an agent working for the owner, not as a data vendor. The scarce input is not scanning but acquiring legally owned physical copies of niche material at scale, and the certificate is what counsel actually buys.
first_30_days: Spend about $25k on a hydraulic cutter and two production scanners. Buy about 10,000 books from library Friends sales and estate lots in one domain (for example legal treatises). Run a 5,000-book pilot for a legal-AI or medical-AI startup, using a custody-certificate template reviewed by copyright counsel.

title: Standby Mass-Fatality Cooler Network for Counties
one_liner: A retainer-based network of vetted funeral homes with cooler space, vans and chain-of-custody training that counties and hospital coalitions can activate when the morgue overflows.
customer: County emergency managers, medical examiner and coroner offices, regional Health Care Coalitions and hospital systems. They fund it through preparedness grants, state emergency-management budgets and hospital readiness budgets.
problem: Mass-fatality plans routinely say 'coordinate with local funeral directors', which is a handshake with no contract, no capacity inventory, no shared identification protocol and no payment. ME planning guides size storage at roughly 1.5x average daily caseload plus a 25% surge buffer, so a heat wave, hurricane, flood or outbreak blows through it. Counties then scramble for refrigerated trailers, which are undignified, poorly tracked, and a magnet for misidentification scandals. Funeral homes are willing to help but can't say what they can commit and dread not being paid.
solution: Enroll 10-30 funeral homes per region. Run a capacity survey (cooler slots, bariatric capability, generators, on-call staff, vehicles). Train them in ID and chain-of-custody basics, personal-effects logging and family-notification etiquette, a DMORT-lite curriculum. Credential their licenses and insurance. Provide a shared dashboard and case-tracking app with unique IDs, tags, photos and effects logs that exports to the ME's systems. Sell the county or coalition a one-to-three-year readiness retainer with an annual tabletop exercise and pre-negotiated per-diem activation rates. Add an 'everyday overflow' service for ME backlogs, such as holiday weekends and opioid or heat spikes, at per-case rates, which turns readiness into recurring revenue.
why_now: Federal disaster support is being pushed toward states and counties, so local preparedness is becoming a locally funded line item. Record heat deaths in the Southwest and busy hurricane seasons keep overloading morgues. ME offices are visibly overflowing, and new facilities such as Jacksonville's in 2026 are being built with triple capacity. Forensic pathologist shortages slow releases and keep bodies in coolers longer.
revenue_model: Annual readiness retainer of $15,000-$60,000 per county or coalition region, with a stipend of about $3,000-$8,000 flowing to each participating funeral home. Activation per diem of $75-$150 per body per day. Overflow per-case fees. $8,000-$15,000 for tabletop exercises and training. Software license for the tracking app.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset in a mass-fatality event isn't refrigerated trucks, it's trusted, licensed humans with cooled rooms already in every zip code, and they sit about 70% idle. No one has ever paid funeral homes to stay ready. Public trust collapses over identification and chain-of-custody errors, not storage, and funeral directors are the only civilians who do that work every day.
first_30_days: Pick one heat- and hurricane-exposed region. Recruit 10-15 funeral homes through the state funeral directors' association. Write a 12-page letter-of-commitment and capacity template. Book meetings with five county emergency managers and two Health Care Coalition coordinators (public directories). Offer a $7,500 paid tabletop exercise plus regional capacity map, priced under many small-purchase thresholds. Convert the exercise participants to a retainer proposal.

title: Notary Network as the Proof-of-Human Layer for Hiring
one_liner: Use the millions of already-commissioned notaries as in-person witnesses who certify that a remote job candidate is a real, physically present person and not a deepfake or proxy.
customer: Security and talent-acquisition leads at remote-first companies (50-2,000 employees) hiring engineers, finance and IT-admin roles, plus crypto and fintech firms, staffing agencies and BPOs onboarding remote workers. Paid per candidate.
problem: Real-time face-swap tools, proxy interviewees and North Korean IT-worker schemes (with DOJ takedowns of US 'laptop farms' in 2025) defeat video interviews and selfie-liveness KYC. Gartner has predicted that one in four candidate profiles could be fake by 2028. Big companies have reportedly brought back in-person final rounds, but a 60-person remote startup has no office to bring anyone to.
solution: A dispatch flow on top of existing mobile-notary and signing-agent networks. The candidate meets a notary in person, at a UPS Store, coworking space or their home. The notary checks physical ID and signs a jurat-style attestation, and the candidate's device is paired to a session key. The notary sits with them for the proctored final technical interview, or witnesses laptop receipt and first login. The employer receives a signed, legally meaningful 'Verified Human Presence' certificate to attach to the ATS, HRIS and payroll. Priced at $79-149 per candidate, with the notary paid $40-70.
why_now: Deepfake fraud in hiring became a mainstream security topic in 2025-26. Enforcement actions against laptop farms have made boards care. Remote-notary and mobile-notary dispatch marketplaces already have the workflow tooling, and ATS platforms now expose APIs and partner directories. Digital-identity vendors are all software-only and share the same weakness against generative video.
revenue_model: Per-verification fee; an ATS-integration subscription (Greenhouse, Ashby, Lever); annual re-verification for employees with privileged access; enterprise bundles for staffing agencies and BPOs.
non_obvious_insight: Notaries are the only large, already-bonded, already-commissioned network of humans whose legal job is to certify that a person was physically in front of them. Identity vendors overlooked them because they assumed software would replace presence. When faces become forgeable, presence attestation becomes the premium product, and the distribution network already exists and needs no capital to build.
first_30_days: Build a simple booking and attestation web flow. Sign up two mobile-notary networks or about 40 individual notaries across SF, NYC, Austin, Seattle and Chicago. Recruit 15-20 security-conscious remote-first startups through CISO and hiring-fraud communities. Charge $99 and complete 50 verifications. Publish anonymized 'fraud caught' case studies to drive inbound.

title: SOC 2 for Rent-Pricing Algorithms
one_liner: An independent audit and continuous-monitoring attestation proving an operator's revenue-management tool uses lawful inputs and real human decisions.
customer: Multifamily operators (5,000-100,000 units) using RealPage, Yardi or Entrata-style pricing in ban or enforcement jurisdictions, defendants under consent decrees needing monitors, and their insurers and lenders.
problem: Pricing tools are now legal liabilities: New York State (Dec 2025) and Berkeley ban them, San Diego levies $1,000 per violation and a UDR class action was filed, private settlements exceed $500M, and Pinnacle signed a decree Sept 4 with Camden the lone unsettled original defendant. Vendors named in suits cannot credibly certify themselves, and operators cannot prove where prices come from.
solution: Audit data lineage (any nonpublic competitor inputs, data age), analyze auto-accept and override rates and human-decision documentation, map jurisdictional exposure, and issue a signed attestation with quarterly evidence reports. License the tooling to monitors of consent decrees.
why_now: Decrees can require compliance officers and monitors, city bans are multiplying, and insurers and lenders are beginning to ask for proof.
revenue_model: $20-60K annual attestation per operator, monitor tool licenses, and insurer or broker referral arrangements.
non_obvious_insight: Independence is the product, and vendors in litigation cannot sell it. As with SOC 2 in cloud, the standard will belong to whoever writes v1 and gets insurers and lenders to accept it. Acceptance rates are the observable that plaintiffs and monitors will use.
first_30_days: Draft a 'Rent Pricing Compliance Standard v0.1' with antitrust counsel. Offer a free exposure scan to 30 operators and sign three paid design partners at a $10K discount. Approach two monitor firms and a D&O broker.
